Codes, turns and hidden pictures

Explain each code, picture or ordering rule before selecting an answer.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Read scaled charts and compare results. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can use codes and alphabet order.
  • I can follow turns and ranking clues.
  • I can find a hidden figure or picture rule.
  • I can list possible pairs without missing any.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Crack a letter code

Look for the rule first. In this code each letter moves 1 step forward.

R becomes S, O becomes P, A becomes B and D becomes E.

ROAD is written SPBE.

Screen 2 of 4

Dictionary order

Compare the first letters. If they match, compare the next letters.

INK, KITE, LAMP, PIN, SUN is in dictionary order.

Say the alphabet in your head to check.

Screen 3 of 4

Follow the moves

Read each command and move one square.

Walls block the way.

Plan the whole route before you run it.

Screen 4 of 4

List every pair

3 shirts and 2 caps make 3 × 2 = 6 outfits.

List the outfits in order so none are missed or repeated.

An array can help you count them.

Words to know
code
A rule that changes letters or numbers into new ones.
dictionary order
Ordering words by their first letter, then second letter and so on.
combination
One choice from each group, like a shirt and a cap.

For parents

What your child learns

Days repeat every 7. If the day before yesterday was Thursday, today is Saturday. A series follows a rule such as adding 6. Codes move letters by a rule that you can find.

A common slip

Children often count from the wrong day. Find today first. For codes, compare each letter position and test the rule on every letter.

5-minute home activity: Crack the code

  1. Write a short word and shuffle the letters by a rule.
  2. Show the word and the code to someone.
  3. Ask them to find the rule.
  4. Write a number series that adds 6 and find the next number.
